Both the [DAVE plotting guide](plotting_dave.html) and the
[runner outputs guide](runner_outputs.html) use **dimensions** to describe which
model prediction a value belongs to. The same concepts apply when plotting in
R or exploring outputs in Shiny.

## Values and dimensions

A value answers **what was predicted, and what was its value?** For example, a
soil water mass output might contain `wmass = 12`. Dimensions answer **where,
when, and for which part of the model?** That value might describe one soil
layer in one patch on one day.

The reader functions return long-form tables: `variable` holds the literal
column name (such as `wmass`) and `value` holds its value. Other columns
identify its time, location, model dimensions, and source simulation. Several
predictions can share a date while belonging to different patches, layers, or
simulations.

Model dimensions depend on the output file. Common identifiers include:

| Columns | What they identify |
| --- | --- |
| `Lon`, `Lat` | The model grid cell's coordinates. |
| `stand` | The stand represented by the row. |
| `patch` | The patch represented by the row. |
| `pft` | The plant functional type, when the file identifies PFTs in rows. |
| `indiv` | The model individual identifier recorded by the output. |
| `layer` | The soil layer, using the file's layer index. |

Identifiers must be interpreted together with the other dimensions and the
simulation they belong to. For example, patch 0 in one simulation is a separate
series from patch 0 in another.

## The column dimension

The plotting APIs call the data dimension `column`; its name in the
reader's long-form table is `variable`.

Some files have a separate data column for each PFT, plus a `total` column. In
that layout, use `column` to distinguish those series. A `pft` dimension is
available only when the original file contains an explicit `pft` identifier
column (typically only in cohort-level outputs).

## Facets, colours, and lines

`facet` chooses which dimensions divide a plot into panels. `colour` chooses
one dimension whose values distinguish colours. For example, `facet = "layer"`
and `colour = "column"` puts each soil layer in its own panel and colours the
different data columns within each panel.

Changing those controls does not aggregate predictions. If a file contains
several patches, their lines remain separate even when they share a panel and
colour. Use the reader and an explicit aggregation step when you need a patch
mean or another summary.

The source also contributes dimensions. DAVE outputs have `repo` and `site`;
runner outputs have `instruction_file`, `simulation`, and `run_id`. Runner
parameter overrides provide additional `param:*` dimensions, explained in the
[parameter overrides section](runner_outputs.html#inspect-and-filter-parameter-overrides).
Output identity is available as `output` in both APIs. These dimensions can be
used alongside the model dimensions for facets and colours.

For worked examples, continue with the
[DAVE panels and colours](plotting_dave.html#choose-the-panels-and-colours) or
[runner simulation comparisons](runner_outputs.html#plot-and-compare-simulations).
